mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A's own shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR ratio (all-prior and recent-5) jointly with Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST rate. The mechanism asks whether the combination of a low on-target conversion rate (Team A) meeting a low shots-on-target concession rate (Team B) produces a jointly suppressed on-target output beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's shots-to-shots-on-target ratio is low (many shots, few on target) AND the opponent suppresses shots-on-target at a below-average rate, the combined on-target output is suppressed more than either factor alone would suggest — a joint multiplicative suppression rather than additive.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) is jointly compared against Team B's defensive suppression of shots-on-target allowed, to test whether a team that generates many shots but converts few on target faces a structurally tighter defensive filter than its raw shot volume implies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly relating two distinct observables (shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR for one team, shots_on_target AGAINST for the other) simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; it is an asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable joint relationship.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on whether Team B's recent-5 possession exceeds its all-prior possession AND its recent-5 shots FOR exceeds its all-prior shots FOR simultaneously. The joint co-movement of both observables in the same direction (upward) defines a 'regime shift' condition distinct from either observable drifting alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both possession and shot volume rise together in recent matches relative to the long-run baseline, the team's shots_on_target FOR also rises — the joint upward regime in two observables is associated with a compounding rather than additive improvement in on-target output.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession dominance (FOR all-prior vs recent-5 showing an upward trend) is jointly related to its shot volume surge (shots FOR recent-5 well above all-prior), testing whether possession expansion and shot-volume expansion co-occur as a reinforcing regime shift rather than independently.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable regime structure (possession AND shots both trending up simultaneously) rather than a single observable's recent vs long-run comparison. The engine covers each observable's recent vs long-run split individually but not their joint co-movement as a regime condition.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A's goals FOR first-half vs second-half split simultaneously with Team B's goals AGAINST first-half vs second-half split. The mechanism tests the cross-team, cross-half asymmetry: Team A scores more in H1 (0.674 vs 0.581) while Team B concedes more in H2 (0.548 vs 0.411). The joint pattern — attacker peaks early, defender leaks late — is the conditioning structure.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the attacking team's goal production is front-loaded (higher H1 than H2) but the defending team's concession rate is back-loaded (higher H2 than H1), the within-match goal distribution is more uniform than either half-split alone implies — the mismatch partially cancels rather than compounds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetry between Team A's first-half goal production and second-half goal production (FOR) is jointly tested against Team B's first-half vs second-half goal concession asymmetry (AGAINST), to identify whether a team that scores more in the first half meets a defence that concedes more in the second half — creating a half-period mismatch in when goals are most likely.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct half-level splits from two different teams on different observables (Team A goals FOR by half, Team B goals AGAINST by half). It is an asymmetric cross-team within-match state relationship, not a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A's corners FOR H1 vs H2 (1.973 vs 2.432 — back-loaded) jointly with Team B's corners AGAINST H1 vs H2 (2.284 vs 2.985 — also back-loaded). The joint back-loading of both attacker production and defender concession in the same half defines a compounding second-half corner pressure condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both the attacking team's corner production and the defending team's corner concession are back-loaded into the second half, total corner volume in the second half rises above what either team's individual half-split would predict in isolation — a compounding rather than independent effect.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team A's corner-kick production split by half (FOR first-half vs second-half) and Team B's corner-kick concession split by half (AGAINST first-half vs second-half) tests whether the within-match corner distribution for Team A aligns or misaligns with the half in which Team B is most vulnerable to conceding corners.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct half-level splits from two different teams on the same observable (corners), creating a cross-team within-match state structure. The engine covers each team's corner rate individually and by venue, but not the joint half-period alignment between attacker production and defender concession.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A's fouls FOR recent-5 being substantially below its all-prior average (8.2 vs 12.86) simultaneously with Team B's yellow_cards FOR recent-5 being substantially above its all-prior average (2.8 vs 1.562). The joint condition — one team in a low-foul regime, the other in a high-card regime — is the cross-team, cross-observable conditioning structure tested against cards_2h outcomes.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the home team is in a low-foul regime and the away team is in a high-card-accumulation regime simultaneously, second-half card volume (cards_2h) is asymmetrically distributed toward the away team rather than being symmetric around the competition baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent-5 foul rate (FOR) has dropped sharply below its all-prior average while Team B's yellow-card rate (FOR) has risen sharply in recent matches. The joint relationship between one team's foul-rate regime shift and the opponent's card-accumulation regime shift tests whether a disciplinary asymmetry — one team fouling less while the other is being carded more — is associated with a divergence in second-half card volume (cards_2h).
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) from two different teams, both in regime-shift states (recent vs long-run divergence), and relates them to a third observable (cards_2h) at half resolution. It is not reducible to any single observable's recent vs long-run comparison or a single observable with one band.
